title.zh: 卷二百四十六 列傳第一百三十四 滿朝薦 江秉謙 侯震暘 王允成
title.en: Volume 246 Biographies 134: Man Chaojian, Jiang Bingqian, Hou Zhenyang, Wang Yuncheng
title.raw: 卷二百四十六 列傳第一百三十四 滿朝薦 江秉謙 侯震暘 王允成 Volume 246 Biographies 134: Man Chaojian, Jiang Bingqian, Hou Zhenyang, Wang Yuncheng

sentences.zh: 滿朝薦江秉謙侯震旸

translations.literal: Man Chaojian, Jiang Bingqian, Hou Zhenyáng.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chaojian, Jiang Bingqian, and Hou Zhenyáng.

sentences.zh: 〈（倪思輝朱欽相王心一）〉

translations.literal: (Ni Sihui, Zhu Qinxiang, Wang Xinyi)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (with the biographies of Ni Sihui, Zhu Qinxiang, and Wang Xinyi)]〉

sentences.zh: 王允成

translations.literal: Wang Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuncheng

sentences.zh: 〈（李希孔毛士龍）〉

translations.literal: (Li Xikong, Mao Shilong)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (with the biographies of Li Xikong and Mao Shilong)]〉

sentences.zh: 滿朝薦，字震東，麻陽人。

translations.literal: Man Chaojian, style name Zhendong, was a native of Mayang.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chaojian, courtesy name Zhendong, came from Mayang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1604.

sentences.zh: 授咸寧知縣，有廉能聲。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xianning and gained a reputation for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Xianning, he soon won a name for clean and capable government.

sentences.zh: 稅監梁永縱其下劫諸生橐，朝薦捕治之。

translations.literal: The tax commissioner Liang Yong let his subordinates rob the purses of degree-holders; Chaojian arrested and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: When the tax commissioner Liang Yong allowed his men to rob local scholars, Chaojian seized and punished the culprits.

sentences.zh: 永怒，劾其擅刑稅役，詔鐫一官。

translations.literal: Yong was enraged and memorialized that Chaojian had illegally punished tax personnel; an edict demoted him one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yong struck back with a memorial accusing Chaojian of unlawfully punishing tax agents, and the throne demoted him one grade.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈鯉等論救，不聽。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries including Shen Li petitioned for leniency, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries such as Shen Li pleaded for him, but the emperor refused to relent.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫顧其誌極論永貪殘狀，乃復朝薦官，奪俸一歲。

translations.literal: When the grand coordinator Gu Qizhi memorialized at length on Yong's greed and cruelty, Chaojian's office was restored, with one year's salary withheld.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Gu Qizhi laid out Yong's greed and brutality in full, Chaojian was reinstated, though his salary was withheld for a year.

sentences.zh: 無何，永遣人蠱巡按御史余懋衡。

translations.literal: Before long, Yong sent someone to bewitch the touring censor Yu Maoheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yong sent men to work sorcery against the touring censor Yu Maoheng.

sentences.zh: 事覺，朝薦捕獲其人。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Chaojian captured the man.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plot was exposed, Chaojian arrested the culprit.

sentences.zh: 永懼，率眾擐甲入縣庭。

translations.literal: Yong in fear led a crowd in armor into the county yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yong marched an armed mob into the county seat.

sentences.zh: 吏卒早為備，無所掠而去。

translations.literal: The clerks and soldiers had made preparations early, so they plundered nothing and left.
translations.idiomatic: The yamen staff had been ready; finding nothing to seize, the mob withdrew.

sentences.zh: 城中數夜驚，言永反，或謂永宜自明，永遂下教，自白不反狀，然蓄甲者數百。

translations.literal: For several nights the city was alarmed, saying Yong had rebelled; some said Yong ought to clear himself, so Yong issued a proclamation stating he was not rebelling, yet he still kept several hundred armed men.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of rebellion kept the city on edge for nights; advised to clear his name, Yong issued a proclamation denying revolt, yet still kept several hundred men under arms.

sentences.zh: 而朝薦助懋衡操之急，諸惡黨多亡去。

translations.literal: Chaojian assisted Maoheng in pressing the case urgently, and many of the evil partisans fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chaojian helped Maoheng press the investigation hard, and most of Yong's ruffians fled.

sentences.zh: 朝薦追之渭南，頗有所格傷。

translations.literal: Chaojian pursued them to Weinan and inflicted considerable casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Chaojian pursued them as far as Weinan and killed or wounded many.

sentences.zh: 永懼，使使系書發中，入都訟朝薦劫上供物，殺數人，投屍河中。

translations.literal: Yong in fear had an envoy tie a letter under his hair and go to the capital to accuse Chaojian of robbing tribute goods, killing several people and throwing the bodies into the river.
translations.idiomatic: In panic Yong sent a courier with a petition hidden in his hair to the capital, charging Chaojian with plundering imperial tribute, murdering several men, and casting the corpses into the river.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，立遣使逮治，時三十五年七月也。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and immediately sent agents to arrest and try him; this was the seventh month of the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and at once dispatched officers to seize him; it was the seventh month of 1607.

sentences.zh: 既至，下詔獄搒掠，遂長系。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was put in the imperial prison and tortured, then long detained.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was thrown into the imperial prison, beaten under interrogation, and held for years.

sentences.zh: 中外論救，自大學士朱賡以下，百十疏。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court memorialized for his release; from Grand Secretary Zhu Geng downward, over a hundred memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Officials across the empire pleaded for mercy; from Grand Secretary Zhu Geng on down, more than a hundred memorials were filed.

sentences.zh: 最後，四十一年秋，萬壽節將屆，用大學士葉向高請，乃與王邦才、卞孔時並釋歸。

translations.literal: Finally, in autumn of the forty-first year, as the empress dowager's birthday approached, at the request of Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao, he was released together with Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.
translations.idiomatic: At last, in the autumn of 1613, as the empress dowager's longevity celebration neared, Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao's petition won their release together with Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起南京刑部郎中，再遷尚寶卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was recalled as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, then promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne, Chaojian was recalled to serve in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，遼東地盡失，海內多故，而廷臣方植黨逞浮議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, Liaodong was entirely lost and the realm was beset with troubles, while courtiers formed factions and indulged in empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: In 1622, with Liaodong lost and the empire in turmoil, courtiers were busy forming factions and trading in hollow debate.

sentences.zh: 朝薦深慮之，疏陳時事十可憂、七可怪，語極危切。

translations.literal: Chaojian was deeply troubled and memorialized on current affairs with ten causes for worry and seven for alarm, his language extremely urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply alarmed, he memorialized listing ten worries and seven portents of the age, in language stark and urgent.

sentences.zh: 尋進太仆少卿，復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, he submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 比者，風霾曀晦，星月晝見，太白經天，四月雹，六月冰，山東地震，畿內霪潦，天地之變極矣。

translations.literal: Recently, dusty haze has dimmed the sky, stars and the moon have been seen by day, Venus has crossed the heavens, hail fell in the fourth month, ice in the sixth, Shandong has suffered earthquake, and the capital region flooding — the changes of Heaven and Earth have reached their extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the sky has hung dark with dust, stars and moon have shone by day, Venus has crossed the heavens, hail has fallen in the fourth month and ice in the sixth, Shandong has quaked and the capital districts have drowned in flood — Heaven and Earth have shown every sign of extremity.

sentences.zh: 四川則奢崇明叛，貴州則安邦彥叛，山東則徐鴻儒亂，民人之變極矣。

translations.literal: In Sichuan She Chongming has rebelled, in Guizhou An Bangyan has rebelled, in Shandong Xu Hongru has risen in disorder — the changes among the people have reached their extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan She Chongming has risen, in Guizhou An Bangyan, in Shandong Xu Hongru — the disorders of the people have reached their extreme as well.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷政令乃顛倒日甚。

translations.literal: Yet the court's commands grow more inverted by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court's policies grow more perverse with every passing day.

sentences.zh: 一乞骸耳，周嘉謨、劉一燝，顧命之元老，以中讒去；

translations.literal: Merely for requesting retirement, Zhou Jiamo and Liu Yijing, elders entrusted at the deathbed, were removed through slander;
translations.idiomatic: Take a single case of requesting retirement: Zhou Jiamo and Liu Yijing, the dying emperor's chosen elders, were driven out on trumped-up charges;

sentences.zh: 孫慎行，守禮之宗伯，以封典去；

translations.literal: Sun Shenxing, the Minister of Rites who upheld ritual, was removed over investiture protocol;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shenxing, a Minister of Rites who stood for propriety, was dismissed over a feudal investiture dispute;

sentences.zh: 王紀，執法如山之司寇，以平反去；

translations.literal: Wang Ji, the Minister of Justice whose enforcement was immovable as a mountain, was removed for quashing a conviction;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, a Minister of Justice famed for unbending enforcement, was cashiered for refusing to execute innocents;

sentences.zh: 皆漠不顧惜。

translations.literal: all were dismissed with indifference.
translations.idiomatic: and the court let them go without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 獨惓惓於三十疏劾之沈纮，即去而猶加異數焉。

translations.literal: Yet alone were they zealous for Shen Hong, whom thirty memorials had impeached — even after his dismissal they still granted him extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shen Hong, impeached in thirty memorials, alone was treated with zealous favor; even after leaving office he still received extraordinary marks of grace.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝有是顛倒乎？

translations.literal: Was there such inversion in the reigns of our ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: Did our ancestral emperors ever tolerate such inversion?

sentences.zh: 一建言耳，倪思輝、朱欽相等之削籍，已重箝口之嗟；

translations.literal: Merely for offering advice, Ni Sihui, Zhu Qinxiang and others were struck from the rolls — already a heavy sigh at silenced mouths;
translations.idiomatic: Take a single case of speaking out: Ni Sihui, Zhu Qinxiang, and others were expelled from office, a bitter sign that honest speech had been gagged;

sentences.zh: 周朝瑞、惠世揚等之拂衣，又中一網之計。

translations.literal: Zhou Chaorui, Hui Shiyang and others who cast off their robes and left fell again into a single net.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zhou Chaorui, Hui Shiyang, and others resigned in protest, they too were caught in the same snare.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝有是顛倒乎？

translations.literal: Was there such inversion in the reigns of our ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: Did our ancestral emperors ever tolerate such inversion?

sentences.zh: 一邊策耳，西部索百萬之貲，邊臣猶慮其未飽；

translations.literal: Merely on a frontier policy, the western tribes demand millions in goods and frontier officials still fear they are not satisfied;
translations.idiomatic: Take frontier policy alone: the western allies demand millions in tribute, and border officials still worry it is not enough;

sentences.zh: 健兒乞錙銖之餉，度支尚謂其過奢。

translations.literal: brave soldiers beg for pittance in pay, yet the Ministry of Revenue still calls it extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: while soldiers plead for scraps of pay, the Ministry of Revenue still denounces the cost as lavish.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝有是顛倒乎？

translations.literal: Was there such inversion in the reigns of our ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: Did our ancestral emperors ever tolerate such inversion?

sentences.zh: 一棄城耳，多年議確之犯或以庇厚而緩求，旬日矜疑之輩反以妒深而苛督。

translations.literal: Merely for abandoning a city, offenders long since judged certain may be pursued slowly because of thick patronage, while those suspected for days are harshly pressed because of deep jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Take the abandonment of a single city: men whose guilt was settled years ago escape slowly thanks to powerful patrons, while newcomers under brief suspicion are hounded mercilessly out of spite.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝有是顛倒乎？

translations.literal: Was there such inversion in the reigns of our ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: Did our ancestral emperors ever tolerate such inversion?

sentences.zh: 一緝奸耳，正罪自有常律，平反原無濫條。

translations.literal: Merely in hunting traitors, proper punishment has its fixed statutes and quashing convictions has no loose provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Take the hunt for spies: established law already governs punishment, and there is no blanket clause for reversing verdicts.

sentences.zh: 遼陽之禍，起於袁應泰之大納降人，降人盡占居民婦女，故遼民發憤，招敵攻城。

translations.literal: The disaster at Liaoyang arose from Yuan Yingtai's great intake of surrendered men; the surrendered men seized the women of the inhabitants, so the people of Liaodong in anger invited the enemy to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Liaoyang began when Yuan Yingtai took in masses of surrendered tribesmen who seized local women; enraged, the people of Liaodong opened the gates to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 事發倉卒，未聞有何人獻送之說也。

translations.literal: The affair erupted in haste; one never heard talk of anyone presenting gifts to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The catastrophe struck in sudden confusion; no one then spoke of traitors handing the city to the foe.

sentences.zh: 廣寧之變，起於王化貞之誤信西部，取餉金以啖插而不給卒伍，以故人心離散。

translations.literal: The change at Guangning arose from Wang Huazhen's mistaken trust in the western tribes, taking army funds to feed the Chahar while not paying the troops, so hearts were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The loss of Guangning sprang from Wang Huazhen's misplaced faith in the western allies: he spent army funds bribing the Chahar while starving his own troops, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 敵兵過河，又不聞西部策應，遂至手足無措，抱頭鼠竄。

translations.literal: When enemy troops crossed the river, again one did not hear of support from the western tribes; they reached the point of helplessness and fled like rats clutching their heads.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy crossed the river no western aid appeared; officers were left helpless and fled in panic like rats.

sentences.zh: 亦事發倉卒，未聞有何人獻送之說也。

translations.literal: This too erupted in haste; one never heard talk of anyone presenting gifts to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That disaster too came in sudden chaos; again no one spoke of traitors handing over the city.

sentences.zh: 深求奸細，不過為化貞卸罪地耳。

translations.literal: Probing deeply for spies is nothing but making room to shift blame from Huazhen.
translations.idiomatic: The fevered hunt for spies is only a way to shift blame onto others and absolve Huazhen.

sentences.zh: 王紀不欲殺人媚人，反致削籍。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, unwilling to kill people to please others, was instead struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, who refused to kill innocents to please the powerful, was himself expelled from office.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝有是顛倒乎？

translations.literal: Was there such inversion in the reigns of our ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: Did our ancestral emperors ever tolerate such inversion?

sentences.zh: 若夫閣臣之職，在主持清議。

translations.literal: As for the duty of grand secretaries, it lies in upholding pure discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries exist to uphold honest debate at court.

sentences.zh: 今章疏有妒才壞政者，非惟不斥也，輕則兩可，重則竟行其言矣。

translations.literal: Now when memorials come from those jealous of talent and ruining government, they are not only not rejected; lightly they receive equivocation, heavily their words are actually carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Today memorials from men who envy talent and wreck policy are not rebuked; at best the court wavers, at worst it enacts their proposals outright.

sentences.zh: 有殛奸報國者，非惟不納也，輕則見讓，重則遞加黜罰矣。

translations.literal: When there are those who would execute traitors to serve the state, they are not only not accepted; lightly they are reproached, heavily they receive successive demotions and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials urging execution of traitors for the nation's sake are not welcomed; mildly their authors are scolded, severely they are demoted again and again.

sentences.zh: 尤有恨者，沈纮賄盧受得進，及受敗，又交通跋扈之奄以樹威。

translations.literal: Most hateful of all, Shen Hong bribed Lu Shou to gain advancement; when Shou fell, he again colluded with overbearing eunuchs to build power.
translations.idiomatic: Worst of all, Shen Hong bought his rise by bribing Lu Shou; when Shou fell, he courted overbearing eunuchs to build a private power base.

sentences.zh: 振、瑾僨裂之禍，皆纮作俑，而放流不加。

translations.literal: The disasters of Wang Zhen and Liu Jin that split the state were all pioneered by Hong, yet exile was not imposed on him.
translations.idiomatic: The catastrophes of Wang Zhen and Liu Jin that nearly tore the dynasty apart were Shen Hong's handiwork, yet he was never banished.

sentences.zh: 他若戚畹，豈不當檢，何至以閹寺之讒，斃其三仆？

translations.literal: As for other imperial in-laws, ought they not be restrained? How could it reach the point that on eunuchs' slander three of their servants were beaten to death?
translations.idiomatic: Other imperial in-laws surely deserved scrutiny; how could eunuch slander end with three of their servants beaten to death?

sentences.zh: 三宮分有常尊，何至以傾國之昵，僭逼母儀。

translations.literal: The three palaces each have their fixed dignity; how could an intimacy that overturns the state usurp and press upon the empress's station?
translations.idiomatic: The three inner palaces each have their proper rank — how could a nursemaid's state-shaking favor usurp the empress's dignity?

sentences.zh: 此皆顛倒之甚者也。

translations.literal: These are all extreme inversions.
translations.idiomatic: These are among the gravest inversions of all.

sentences.zh: 顧成於陛下者什之一二，成於當事大臣者十之八九。

translations.literal: Yet what is accomplished by Your Majesty is one or two parts in ten; what is accomplished by the ministers in charge is eight or nine parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only one or two parts in ten of this disorder springs from Your Majesty; eight or nine parts spring from the ministers who hold power.

sentences.zh: 臣誠不忍見神州陸沈，祈陛下終覽臣疏，與閣部大臣更弦易轍，悉軌祖宗舊章，臣即從逢、幹於地下，猶生之年。

translations.literal: Your servant truly cannot bear to see the divine land sink; I pray Your Majesty will finally peruse my memorial, change course with the grand secretaries and ministers, wholly follow the old statutes of the ancestors — then even if I follow Peng and Gan in the underworld, it will be as the years of life.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to watch the empire sink; I beg Your Majesty to read this memorial through, change course with the Grand Secretariat and ministry heads, and return wholly to the ancestral statutes — then even if I join the loyal dead underground, I shall count myself among the living.

sentences.zh: 既奏，魏忠賢激帝怒，降旨切責，褫職為民。

translations.literal: Once it was submitted, Wei Zhongxian stirred the emperor's anger; an edict sharply rebuked him and stripped him of office, making him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was in, Wei Zhongxian inflamed the emperor's wrath; an edict sharply rebuked Chaojian and reduced him to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 大學士向高申救甚力，帝不納。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xiang Gao pleaded for him with great force, but the emperor would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao pleaded vigorously for him, but the emperor would not relent.

sentences.zh: 已，忠賢黨撰《東林同誌錄》，朝薦與焉，竟不復用。

translations.literal: Later the Zhongxian faction compiled 《Record of Donglin Comrades》; Chaojian was listed therein and was never employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhongxian's faction compiled 《Register of Donglin Comrades》; Chaojian was named in it and never served again.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年薦起故官，未上卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recommended to his former office but died before taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1629 he was recommended to his old post but died before he could report.

sentences.zh: 江秉謙，字兆豫，歙人。

translations.literal: Jiang Bingqian, style name Zhaoyu, was a native of She in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bingqian, courtesy name Zhaoyu, came from She in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1610.

sentences.zh: 除鄞縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 用廉能征，擬授御史。

translations.literal: Summoned for integrity and competence, he was slated to receive appointment as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital for his clean record, he was slated for a censor's post.

sentences.zh: 久不得命，以葬親歸。

translations.literal: For long he did not receive the order and returned home to bury his parent.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was long delayed, and he went home to bury a parent.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，命始下，入臺，侃侃言事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, the order finally came down; he entered the Censorate and spoke forthrightly on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne the appointment finally arrived; he entered the Censorate and spoke his mind plainly.

sentences.zh: 沈陽既失，朝士多思熊廷弼，而給事中郭鞏獨論廷弼喪師誤國，請並罪閣臣劉一燝。

translations.literal: Once Shenyang was lost, many at court thought of Xiong Tingbi, but Supervising Secretary Guo Gong alone argued that Tingbi had lost the army and misled the state, requesting that Grand Secretary Liu Yijing also be punished.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenyang fell many officials looked to Xiong Tingbi to save Liaodong, but Supervising Secretary Guo Gong alone blamed Tingbi for losing the army and asked that Grand Secretary Liu Yijing be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 秉謙憤，力頌廷弼保守危疆功，且曰：「今廷弼勘覆已明，議者猶以一人私情沒天下公論，寧壞朝廷封疆，不忘胸中畛域。」

translations.literal: Bingqian was indignant and strongly praised Tingbi's merit in holding a perilous frontier, saying: "Now Tingbi's investigation and review are already clear, yet critics still let one man's private feeling drown the public opinion of the realm, preferring to ruin the court's borders rather than forget the boundaries in their breasts."
translations.idiomatic: Bingqian was furious and vigorously praised Tingbi for holding the frontier in crisis, saying: "Tingbi's case has already been cleared, yet critics still let private spite drown the public good — they would rather wreck the empire's defenses than lay aside personal grudges."

sentences.zh: 章下廷議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for court discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to a court conference.

sentences.zh: 會遼陽復失，廷弼旋起經略。

translations.literal: As it happened Liaoyang was lost again and Tingbi was soon raised as frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liaoyang fell again and Tingbi was at once reappointed frontier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鞏坐妄議奪官，遂與秉謙為仇。

translations.literal: Gong was punished for reckless discussion by loss of office and thus became Bingqian's enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Gong lost his post for reckless criticism and thereafter treated Bingqian as an enemy.

sentences.zh: 廷弼既鎮山海，議遣使宣諭朝鮮發兵牽制。

translations.literal: Once Tingbi was stationed at Shanhai Pass, it was proposed to send an envoy to announce and instruct Korea to raise troops for diversion.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tingbi held Shanhai Pass, the court debated sending an envoy to urge Korea to raise troops and pin down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 副使梁之垣請行，廷弼喜，請付二十萬金為軍貲。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Liang Zhiyuan requested to go; Tingbi was pleased and asked that two hundred thousand taels of gold be provided as army funds.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Liang Zhiyuan volunteered; Tingbi welcomed the mission and asked for two hundred thousand taels in military funds.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張鶴鳴不予，秉謙抗疏爭。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Heming would not grant it; Bingqian submitted a defiant memorial arguing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Heming refused; Bingqian memorialized forcefully in protest.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴怒，力詆秉謙朋黨。

translations.literal: Heming was angry and fiercely denounced Bingqian as a factionalist.
translations.idiomatic: Heming flew into a rage and accused Bingqian of factional scheming.

sentences.zh: 秉謙疏辨，帝不罪。

translations.literal: Bingqian memorialized in defense; the emperor did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Bingqian defended himself in a memorial; the emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴既抑廷弼，專庇巡撫王化貞，朝士多附會之。

translations.literal: Heming, having suppressed Tingbi, devoted himself to shielding Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen, and many courtiers joined in supporting him.
translations.idiomatic: Having sidelined Tingbi, Heming threw his weight behind Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen, and many officials fell in behind him.

sentences.zh: 帝以經、撫不和，詔廷臣議。

translations.literal: Because the commissioner and coordinator were not in harmony, the emperor ordered the court to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, troubled by the feud between commissioner and coordinator, ordered a court debate.

sentences.zh: 秉謙言：「陛下再起廷弼，委以重寄，曰『疆場事不從中制』。

translations.literal: Bingqian said: "Your Majesty raised Tingbi again and entrusted him with heavy responsibility, saying 'Frontier affairs shall not be directed from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Bingqian said: "Your Majesty restored Tingbi and gave him grave responsibility, declaring that frontier affairs would not be micromanaged from the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃數月以來，廷弼不得措手足，呼號日聞，辨駁踵至。

translations.literal: Yet for several months Tingbi has been unable to move hand or foot; cries of distress are heard daily and rebuttals arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for months he has been unable to act; his appeals echo daily and rebuttals pour in one after another.

sentences.zh: 執為詞者曰『經、撫不和，化貞主戰，廷弼主守耳，夫廷弼非專言守，謂守定而後可戰也。

translations.literal: Those who hold to the argument say, 'The commissioner and coordinator are not in harmony; Huazhen advocates battle and Tingbi advocates defense.' But Tingbi does not speak only of defense — he means that once defense is settled one may then fight.
translations.idiomatic: The excuse offered is that commissioner and coordinator disagree — Huazhen favors attack, Tingbi defense. Yet Tingbi does not preach defense alone; he means that once defenses are firm, attack becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 化貞銳意戰，即戰勝，可無事守乎？

translations.literal: Huazhen is keen to fight — even if he wins, can there be no need for defense?
translations.idiomatic: Huazhen is eager to fight — even if he wins, will defense no longer matter?

sentences.zh: 萬一不勝，又將何以守？

translations.literal: If by chance he does not win, how then will he defend?
translations.idiomatic: And if he loses, how will the frontier be held?

sentences.zh: 此中利害，夫人知之。

translations.literal: The advantage and harm in this — every man knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Every man at court knows the stakes.

sentences.zh: 乃一則無言不從，一則無策不棄。

translations.literal: Yet to one side not a word goes unheeded, to the other not a plan goes unabandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huazhen's every word is obeyed while Tingbi's every plan is cast aside.

sentences.zh: 豈真不明於戰守之說，但從化貞、廷弼起見耳。

translations.literal: How could they truly not understand the discourse of fighting and defending? They only take their stand from favoring Huazhen or Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: They are not ignorant of strategy; they simply take sides between Huazhen and Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 陛下既命廷弼節制三方，則三方之進戰退守當一一聽其指揮。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty has ordered Tingbi to command the three sectors, the advance, battle, retreat and defense of the three sectors ought each to heed his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty placed Tingbi in command of all three sectors; every advance, battle, retreat, and defense ought to follow his orders.

sentences.zh: 乃化貞欲進，則使廷弼從之進，欲退，則使廷弼隨之退。

translations.literal: Yet when Huazhen wishes to advance, Tingbi is made to advance with him; when he wishes to retreat, Tingbi is made to retreat with him.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, when Huazhen advances Tingbi must follow; when Huazhen retreats Tingbi must follow.

sentences.zh: 化貞倏進倏退，則使廷弼進不知所以戰，退不知所以守。

translations.literal: Huazhen suddenly advances and suddenly retreats, so that Tingbi, advancing, does not know how to fight, and retreating, does not know how to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhen lurches forward and back, leaving Tingbi unsure how to fight when advancing or how to defend when retreating.

sentences.zh: 是化貞有節制廷弼之權，而廷弼未嘗有節制三方之權也。

translations.literal: Thus Huazhen has the power to command Tingbi, while Tingbi has never had the power to command the three sectors.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhen commands Tingbi, yet Tingbi has never truly commanded the three sectors.

sentences.zh: 故今日之事，非經、撫不和，乃好惡經、撫者不和；

translations.literal: Therefore today's affair is not that commissioner and coordinator are not in harmony, but that those who favor or hate the commissioner and coordinator are not in harmony;
translations.idiomatic: Today's trouble is not discord between commissioner and coordinator, but discord among those who take sides for or against them;

sentences.zh: 非戰守之議論不合，乃左右經、撫者之議論不合。

translations.literal: It was not that opinions on fighting and defending did not agree, but that the opinions of those flanking them—the circuit intendant and the grand coordinator—did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The deadlock was not over strategy itself—whether to attack or hold—but over the feud between the frontier commanders, the circuit intendant and the grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 請專責廷弼，實圖戰守。」

translations.literal: They requested that sole responsibility be placed on Tingbi, with a sincere plan for both war and defense.'
translations.idiomatic: They urged that Xiong Tingbi be given undivided authority and a genuine mandate to prosecute both offense and defense."

sentences.zh: 末譏首輔葉向高兩可含糊，勢必兩可掣肘，安能責成功。

translations.literal: At the end he mocked Chief Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao for being equivocal on both sides, saying that such ambiguity was bound to hamstring both courses—how could success be demanded?
translations.idiomatic: In closing he ridiculed Chief Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao for straddling both camps; such fence-sitting would only tie everyone's hands—how could victory be expected?

sentences.zh: 語極切至。

translations.literal: His words were extremely pointed.
translations.idiomatic: The language was unsparing in its bluntness.

sentences.zh: 後朝議方撤廷弼，而化貞已棄廣寧遁。

translations.literal: Later, when the court was just debating the removal of Tingbi, Huazhen had already abandoned Guangning and fled.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the court began deliberating Xiong Tingbi's dismissal, Wang Huazhen had already fled and surrendered Guangning.

sentences.zh: 秉謙益憤，以職方郎耿如杞附和鶴鳴，力助化貞排廷弼，致封疆喪失，連疏攻之。

translations.literal: Bingqian grew all the more furious; because the Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments Geng Ruqi had echoed Heming and vigorously aided Huazhen in driving out Tingbi, causing the loss of the frontier, he submitted successive memorials attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bingqian's outrage only deepened. Geng Ruqi of the Bureau of Military Appointments had sided with Zhang Heming, abetted Wang Huazhen, and helped oust Xiong Tingbi—directly contributing to the loss of the borderlands—so Bingqian hammered them in memorial after memorial.

sentences.zh: 並援世宗戮丁汝夔故事，乞亟置鶴鳴於法。

translations.literal: He moreover cited the precedent of Emperor Shizong's execution of Ding Ruao, requesting that Heming be immediately brought to justice under the law.
translations.idiomatic: He invoked the precedent of the Jiajing Emperor's execution of Ding Ruao and demanded that Zhang Heming be swiftly tried and punished.

sentences.zh: 帝以鶴鳴方行邊，不當輕詆，奪秉謙俸半歲，如杞不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor, on the grounds that Heming was then touring the frontier and ought not be lightly slandered, stripped Bingqian of half a year's salary and did not inquire into Ruqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ruled that Zhang Heming, being on an inspection tour of the frontier, should not be lightly maligned; he docked Zhou Bingqian half a year's pay and took no action against Geng Ruqi.

sentences.zh: 秉謙復上疏言：「鶴鳴一入中樞，初不過鹵莽而無遠識，既乃至兇狠而動殺機。

translations.literal: Bingqian again submitted a memorial saying: "Once Heming entered the central administration, at first he was merely reckless and lacked far-sightedness; subsequently he became fiercely cruel and moved to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bingqian submitted another memorial: "From the moment Zhang Heming entered the inner circle of power, he was crude and shortsighted; before long he had turned vicious and begun plotting lives.

sentences.zh: 明知西部間諜俱虛，戰守參差難合，乃顧自欺以欺朝廷。

translations.literal: Knowing full well that the western frontier's spies were all false reports and that plans for war and defense were mismatched and hard to reconcile, he nevertheless chose to deceive himself in order to deceive the court.
translations.idiomatic: He knew perfectly well that western intelligence was worthless and that offensive and defensive plans could never be aligned—yet he chose self-deception as his means of deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 何處有機會？

translations.literal: Where was there any opportunity?
translations.idiomatic: Where, in truth, was any opening to be found?

sentences.zh: 而曰機會可乘。

translations.literal: Yet he said an opportunity could be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he declared that the moment was ripe.

sentences.zh: 何日渡河？

translations.literal: On what day would they cross the river?
translations.idiomatic: When were they ever to cross the river?

sentences.zh: 而曰渡河必勝。

translations.literal: Yet he said that crossing the river would surely bring victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he insisted that crossing would guarantee triumph.

sentences.zh: 既欲驅經略以出關，而不肯付經略以節制，既欲置廷弼於廣寧，而未嘗移化貞於何地。

translations.literal: Having wished to drive the frontier commissioner beyond the pass yet being unwilling to grant him command authority; having wished to place Tingbi at Guangning yet never having moved Huazhen anywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to drive the frontier commissioner beyond the pass but refused to grant him full command; he meant to station Xiong Tingbi at Guangning but never said where Wang Huazhen was to be redeployed.

sentences.zh: 破壞封疆之罪，可置弗問哉？

translations.literal: The crime of ruining the frontier territory—could it be left unpunished?
translations.idiomatic: Could the crime of wrecking the realm's borders simply be ignored?

sentences.zh: 且化貞先棄地先逃，猶曰功罪相半。

translations.literal: Moreover, Huazhen had been first to abandon the territory and first to flee, yet they still said his merits and faults were equal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huazhen had been the first to abandon his post and flee—yet they still treated merit and fault as equal halves.

sentences.zh: 即此一言，縱寸斬鶴鳴，不足贖其欺君誤國罪，乃猶敢哆口定他入罪案耶！」

translations.literal: By this remark alone, even if Heming were cut into inch-wide pieces, it would not redeem his crime of deceiving the ruler and ruining the state—yet he still dared to open his mouth and decide other men's cases of guilt!
translations.idiomatic: That single utterance alone—even dismembering Zhang Heming inch by inch would not atone for his crimes of deceiving the sovereign and ruining the state—yet he still had the audacity to sit in judgment over others!

sentences.zh: 當是時，大學士沈纮潛結中官劉朝、乳媼客氏，募兵入禁中，興內操。

translations.literal: At that time, Grand Secretary Shen Hong secretly allied with the eunuch Liu Chao and the wet nurse Madam Ke, recruited troops into the Forbidden City, and established inner drill exercises.
translations.idiomatic: At that juncture Grand Secretary Shen Hong had secretly joined forces with the eunuch Liu Chao and the wet nurse Madam Ke, raised troops within the Forbidden City, and instituted inner-court military drills.

sentences.zh: 給事中惠世揚、周朝瑞等十二人再疏力攻，秉謙與焉，並詆朝及客氏。

translations.literal: Twelve supervising secretaries including Hui Shiyang and Zhou Chaorui again submitted memorials fiercely attacking this, Bingqian among them, also denouncing Chao and Madam Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve supervising secretaries, among them Hui Shiyang and Zhou Chaorui, launched fresh memorial assaults—Zhou Bingqian included—also denouncing Liu Chao and Madam Ke.

sentences.zh: 內外胥怨，遂假劾鶴鳴疏，出秉謙於外。

translations.literal: With grievances inside and out, they then used the pretext of the memorial impeaching Heming to send Bingqian out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment festered within the palace and without; under cover of the impeachment of Zhang Heming, they sent Zhou Bingqian away from court.

sentences.zh: 無何，郭鞏召還，交通魏忠賢，力沮秉謙。

translations.literal: Before long, Guo Gong was recalled, colluded with Wei Zhongxian, and strenuously obstructed Bingqian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guo Gong was recalled, cultivated ties with Wei Zhongxian, and worked tirelessly to block Zhou Bingqian's restoration.

sentences.zh: 是冬，皇子生，言官被謫者悉召還，獨秉謙不與。

translations.literal: That winter, when a prince was born, all demoted remonstrating officials were recalled—Bingqian alone was excluded.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, upon the birth of an imperial prince, every demoted remonstrating official was recalled—all except Zhou Bingqian.

sentences.zh: 家居四年，聞忠賢益亂政，憂憤卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for four years, and upon hearing that Zhongxian was further corrupting government, died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: He spent four years in retirement; learning that Wei Zhongxian's tyranny only deepened, he died of anguish.

sentences.zh: 居數月，忠賢黨御史卓邁追劾秉謙保護廷弼，遂削籍。

translations.literal: Several months later, Zhuo Mai, a censor in Zhongxian's faction, pursued a charge against Bingqian for protecting Tingbi, and his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Months after his death, the Wei Zhongxian loyalist censor Zhuo Mai pursued charges against him for shielding Xiong Tingbi, and Zhou Bingqian was posthumously struck from the official register.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen ascended the throne, his official status was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 侯震旸，字得一，嘉定人。

translations.literal: Hou Zhenyáng, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhenyáng, styled Deyi, came from Jiading.

sentences.zh: 祖堯封，監察御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yao Feng was a supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao Feng had served as a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 忤大學士張居正，外轉。

translations.literal: Having offended Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, he was transferred to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, he was posted away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 累官至福建右參政，有廉直聲。

translations.literal: He rose through successive offices to Right Vice Administrator of Fujian, enjoying a reputation for integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Right Vice Administrator of Fujian, where he earned renown for probity and moral courage.

sentences.zh: 震旸舉萬歷三十八年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli and was appointed Gentlemen for Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhenyáng attained jinshi rank in Wanli 38 and received appointment as a Gentlemen for Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was elevated to Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 是時，保姆奉聖夫人客氏方擅寵，與魏忠賢及大學士沈纮相表裏，勢焰張甚。

translations.literal: At that time the wet nurse, the Lady of Fengsheng, Madam Ke, was arrogating favor; with Wei Zhongxian and Grand Secretary Shen Hong she acted in concert inside and out, and her power blazed fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the wet nurse Madam Ke, ennobled as Lady of Fengsheng, held the Emperor's exclusive favor; in league with Wei Zhongxian and Grand Secretary Shen Hong, her faction inside and outside the palace burned with unchecked power.

sentences.zh: 既遣出宮，熹宗思念流涕，至日旰不禦食，遂宣諭復入。

translations.literal: After she had been sent out of the palace, Emperor Xizong missed her to the point of weeping, until the sun slanted westward without his taking a meal; he then issued an edict summoning her back.
translations.idiomatic: When she was dismissed from the palace, Emperor Xizong missed her so deeply he wept; he skipped meals until dusk, then issued an edict calling her back.

sentences.zh: 震旸疏言：「宮闈禁地，奸珰群小睥睨其側，內外鉤連，借叢煬竈，有不忍言者。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng submitted a memorial saying: "The inner palace is forbidden ground; treacherous eunuchs and petty men lurk at its side; inside and outside are hooked together, fanning provocation from a thicket of hearths—there are things too unbearable to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhenyáng memorialized: "The inner quarters are sacred ground, yet wicked eunuchs and petty schemers watch from the margins; palace and court are entangled, stoking one another's fires from a tangle of hidden hearths—there are horrors one scarcely dares name.

sentences.zh: 王聖寵而煽江京、李閏之奸，趙嬈寵而構曹節、皇甫之變。

translations.literal: Wang Sheng's favor fanned the treachery of Jiang Jing and Li Run; Zhao Yao's favor engineered the calamity of Cao Jie and Huangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He favored Wang Sheng and thereby unleashed Jiang Jing and Li Run; Emperor Ling indulged Zhao Yao and thus brought on the disaster of Cao Jie and Huangfu Gui.

sentences.zh: 幺麽裏婦，何堪數昵至尊哉？」

translations.literal: A lowly village woman from the inner rooms—how can she be permitted repeatedly to dally with the Supreme Lord?
translations.idiomatic: A common wet nurse from the women's quarters—how can she be allowed such repeated intimacy with the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 不省。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 會遼事棘，經略熊廷弼、巡撫王化貞相牴牾，兵部尚書張鶴鳴右化貞，議者遂欲移廷弼，與化貞畫地任事。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong affair grew critical, Frontier Commissioner Xiong Tingbi and Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen were at odds; Minister of War Zhang Heming sided with Huazhen, and those in discussion wished to transfer Tingbi and have him and Huazhen divide territory and duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong crisis sharpened: Frontier Commissioner Xiong Tingbi and Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen were at loggerheads. Minister of War Zhang Heming favored Wang Huazhen, and court opinion turned toward removing Xiong Tingbi and having the two men split the territory between them.

sentences.zh: 震旸逆知其必敗，疏言：「事勢至此，陛下宜遣問經臣。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng foresaw in advance that this must fail, and submitted a memorial saying: "Matters have come to this pass; Your Majesty ought to send to inquire of the frontier minister.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhenyáng foresaw disaster and memorialized: "Matters have reached this pass. Your Majesty should summon the frontier commissioner for direct consultation.

sentences.zh: 果能加意訓練，則進止遲速不從中制，雖撤撫臣，一以付之，無不可者。

translations.literal: If he can indeed devote special attention to training, then whether to advance or hold back, swiftly or slowly, should not be controlled from the center—even if the grand coordinator is removed, entrusting everything to him would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If he can truly commit to drill and readiness, then let advance and retreat, timing and tempo, lie entirely in his hands—not directed from the capital. Even dismiss the grand coordinator and give him sole charge—anything is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 如不然，則督其條晰陳奏，以聽吏議，摭拾殘局，專任化貞。

translations.literal: If not, then urge him to set forth his plans clearly in a memorial, hear the officials' deliberation, gather up the broken pieces, and give Huazhen sole responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: If not, demand a detailed written plan, let the ministry debate it, salvage what remains, and put Wang Huazhen in sole command.

sentences.zh: 此一說也。

translations.literal: This is one proposal.
translations.idiomatic: That is one course.

sentences.zh: 不則移廷弼密雲，而出本兵為經略。

translations.literal: Otherwise, transfer Tingbi to Miyun and send out the Minister of War himself as frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, transfer Xiong Tingbi to Miyun and dispatch the Minister of War himself to serve as frontier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴素慷慨自命，與其事敗同罪，不若挺身報國。

translations.literal: Heming has always styled himself a man of bold spirit; to share the guilt of his failed policy is not as good as stepping forward to serve the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heming has always prided himself on heroic ambition—better to share the blame of failure by taking the post himself and serving the realm directly.

sentences.zh: 此又一說也。

translations.literal: This is yet another proposal.
translations.idiomatic: That is another course.

sentences.zh: 不則遂以經略授化貞，擇沈深有謀者代任巡撫，以資後勁。

translations.literal: Otherwise, simply grant the frontier commission to Huazhen, choose someone deep and thoughtful to replace him as grand coordinator, to provide rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Or grant the frontier commission outright to Wang Huazhen and select a seasoned, shrewd man as grand coordinator to sustain the rear.

sentences.zh: 此又一說也。

translations.literal: This is yet another proposal.
translations.idiomatic: That is yet another course.

sentences.zh: 不則直移廷弼於登、萊，終其三方布置之策，與化貞相犄角。

translations.literal: Otherwise, directly transfer Tingbi to Dengzhou and Laizhou, to complete his three-front disposition plan, forming pincers with Huazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Or move Xiong Tingbi directly to Deng and Lai to finish his three-front deployment, forming a pincer with Wang Huazhen.

sentences.zh: 此又一說也。

translations.literal: This is yet another proposal.
translations.idiomatic: That is yet another course.

sentences.zh: 若復遷延猶豫，必僨國事。」

translations.literal: If delay and hesitation continue, the affairs of state will surely be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Further delay and vacillation will surely wreck the nation's fortunes.

sentences.zh: 疏上，方有旨集議，而大清兵已破廣寧矣。

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted, an edict had just been issued to convene discussion, when the Great Qing army had already taken Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial had barely reached the throne and an edict had just been issued to convene debate—when the Qing army already stormed Guangning.

sentences.zh: 化貞、廷弼相率入關門，猶數奉溫旨，責以戴罪立功。

translations.literal: Huazhen and Tingbi led each other through the pass gates; they were still repeatedly granted warm edicts ordering them to atone for their faults through meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huazhen and Xiong Tingbi fled back through the pass together—yet still received gracious edicts bidding them redeem their failures with deeds.

sentences.zh: 震旸大憤懣，再疏言：「臣言不幸驗矣，為今日計，論法不論情。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng was greatly resentful and indignant, and again submitted a memorial saying: "My words have unfortunately been borne out; for today's reckoning, one must judge by law, not sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhenyáng, furious, memorialized again: "My warnings have sadly come true. For the present reckoning, weigh the law—not personal feeling.

sentences.zh: 河西未壞以前，舉朝所惜者，什七在化貞，今不能為化貞惜也。

translations.literal: Before the west of the river was lost, of what the whole court cherished, seven-tenths favored Huazhen; now one cannot spare affection for Huazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Before the western frontier collapsed, the court's sympathies ran seven parts in ten toward Wang Huazhen—today no one can afford such tenderness toward him.

sentences.zh: 河西既壞以後，舉朝所寬者什九在廷弼，今亦不能為廷弼寬也。

translations.literal: After the west of the river was lost, of what the whole court would leniently treat, nine-tenths favored Tingbi; now one cannot afford leniency for Tingbi either.
translations.idiomatic: After the western frontier fell, nine parts in ten of the court's mercy fell on Xiong Tingbi—today even he cannot be spared.

sentences.zh: 策撫臣者，謂宜責令還赴廣寧，聯屬西部。

translations.literal: Those strategizing for the grand coordinator said he ought to be ordered to return to Guangning and link up with the western force.
translations.idiomatic: Those counseling on the grand coordinator argued he should be ordered back to Guangning to reunite with the western allies.

sentences.zh: 然而廥庫已竭，其能赤手效包胥乎？

translations.literal: Yet the granaries and treasuries were already exhausted—could he with bare hands imitate Shen Baoxu?
translations.idiomatic: But the stores were empty—could he, empty-handed, work a miracle like Shen Baoxu?

sentences.zh: 策經臣者，謂宜仍責守關。

translations.literal: Those strategizing for the frontier minister said he ought still to be charged with holding the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Those counseling on the frontier commissioner urged that he still be tasked with holding the passes.

sentences.zh: 然所謂守者，將如廷弼前議三十萬兵數十萬餉，以圖後效乎？

translations.literal: Yet what was meant by holding—was it to be as Tingbi had previously proposed, three hundred thousand troops and several hundred thousand taels of rations, seeking later results?
translations.idiomatic: But what kind of defense was meant—Xiong Tingbi's original plan of three hundred thousand men and a treasury of supplies, aiming for eventual payoff?

sentences.zh: 抑止令率殘卒出關外，姑示不殺乎？

translations.literal: Or merely to order him to lead remnant troops outside the pass, to make a show of not giving up?
translations.idiomatic: Or merely to parade a remnant force beyond the pass as a token gesture of resolve?

sentences.zh: 凡此無一可者。

translations.literal: None of these was feasible.
translations.idiomatic: None of these would suffice.

sentences.zh: 及今不定逃臣之律，殘疆其奚賴焉？」

translations.literal: If the law for fleeing officials is not now fixed, on what can the broken frontier rely?
translations.idiomatic: If the law for absconding officials is not settled now, what hope remains for the shattered borderlands?

sentences.zh: 其後治失事罪，蓋略如震旸疏雲。

translations.literal: Thereafter the handling of punishments for the dereliction of duty largely followed what Zhenyáng's memorial had said.
translations.idiomatic: The subsequent disposition of culpability largely tracked Hou Zhenyáng's memorial.

sentences.zh: 已，遂劾大學士沈纮結納奉聖夫人及諸中官為朋黨，具發其構殺故監王安狀。

translations.literal: Soon after, he impeached Grand Secretary Shen Hong for forming a faction with the Lady of Fengsheng and various eunuchs, fully exposing how he had plotted the killing of the former Director of Ceremonies Wang An.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Grand Secretary Shen Hong for conspiring with Madam Ke, Lady of Fengsheng, and several eunuchs as a clique, laying bare in detail Shen's role in framing and killing the former Director of Ceremonies Wang An.

sentences.zh: 忠賢即日傳旨謫震旸。

translations.literal: Zhongxian that same day transmitted an edict demoting Zhenyáng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian that very day had an edict issued banishing Hou Zhenyáng from office.

sentences.zh: 震旸陛辭，復上田賦、河渠二議。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng, upon taking leave at court, again submitted two proposals on land tax and river works.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience Hou Zhenyáng submitted further proposals on land tax and irrigation.

sentences.zh: 以逐臣不當建議，再鐫二級以歸。

translations.literal: On the grounds that a banished official ought not offer proposals, he was again demoted two ranks and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Because a dismissed official was deemed unfit to counsel, he was stripped of two further ranks and sent home.

sentences.zh: 震旸在垣八月，章奏凡數十上。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng was at the Censorate for eight months and submitted dozens of memorials in all.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhenyáng served at the Censorate for eight months, filing dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，召復故官，震旸已前卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was summoned to restore his former office, but Zhenyáng had already died previously.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen took the throne he was recalled to his former post—but Hou Zhenyáng had already died.

sentences.zh: 因其子主事峒曾請，特贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the request of his son, the Director Zhu Zeng, he was specially granted the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the petition of his son, Director Zhu Zeng, he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 方震旸之論客氏也，給事中祁門倪思輝、臨川朱欽相疏繼之。

translations.literal: When Zhenyáng was memorializing about Madam Ke, the supervising secretaries Ni Sihui of Qimen and Zhu Qinxiang of Linchuan submitted memorials in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Zhenyáng attacked Madam Ke, Supervising Secretaries Ni Sihui of Qimen and Zhu Qinxiang of Linchuan followed with memorials of their own.

sentences.zh: 帝大恚，並貶三官。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and demoted all three officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor erupted in fury and demoted all three.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉一燝、尚書周嘉謨等交章論救，皆不納。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Liu Yizao, Minister Zhou Jiamo, and others submitted successive memorials pleading for them, but none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Yizao, Minister Zhou Jiamo, and others intervened with successive appeals—all rejected.

sentences.zh: 御史吳縣王心一言之尤切，帝怒，貶官如之。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Xinyi of Wuxian spoke with especial force; the Emperor was angered and demoted him in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Xinyi of Wuxian spoke with particular bluntness; the Emperor's wrath fell on him too, and he was demoted likewise.

sentences.zh: 心一同官龍溪馬鳴起復抗疏諫，且言客氏六不可留。

translations.literal: Xinyi's colleague Ma Mingqi of Longxi again submitted a remonstrance in opposition, also stating six reasons Madam Ke should not be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xinyi's colleague Ma Mingqi of Longxi remonstrated again, itemizing six reasons Madam Ke must not remain at court.

sentences.zh: 帝議加重譴，用一燝等言，奪俸一年。

translations.literal: The Emperor deliberated a heavier punishment; accepting the words of Yizao and others, he stripped one year's salary instead.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor considered a harsher penalty but, heeding Liu Yizao and others, settled on stripping one year's salary.

sentences.zh: 欽相尋擢太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Qinxiang was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qinxiang was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 楊漣既劾魏忠賢，欽相亦抗疏極論。

translations.literal: After Yang Lian had impeached Wei Zhongxian, Qinxiang also submitted a fierce memorial of extensive argument.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Zhu Qinxiang too submitted a trenchant memorial of full-throated condemnation.

sentences.zh: 五年以右僉都御史巡撫福建，討賊楊六、蔡三、鐘六等有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Fujian, and achieved merit in suppressing the bandits Yang Liu, Cai San, Zhong Liu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Fujian, earning distinction suppressing the bandits Yang Liu, Cai San, Zhong Liu, and their ilk.

sentences.zh: 旋以忤忠賢，除名。

translations.literal: Soon, for offending Zhongxian, his name was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He soon crossed Wei Zhongxian and was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 思輝，崇禎時終南京督儲尚書，心一終刑部侍郎，鳴起終南京右都御史。

translations.literal: Sihui ended as Minister of Grain Storage at Nanjing in the Chongzhen era; Xinyi ended as Vice Minister of Justice; Mingqi ended as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Sihui ended his career as Nanjing Minister of Grain Storage under Chongzhen; Wang Xinyi as Vice Minister of Justice; Ma Mingqi as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 王允成，字述文，澤州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuncheng, courtesy name Shuwén, was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuncheng, styled Shuwén, came from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉於鄉，除獲鹿知縣。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era he passed the provincial examination and was appointed Magistrate of Huolu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations and was appointed magistrate of Huolu.

sentences.zh: 以治行異等，征授南京御史。

translations.literal: For administrative performance of exceptional grade, he was summoned and appointed Nanjing Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for outstanding governance, he was called to serve as a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 時甲科勢重，乙科多卑下之。

translations.literal: At the time jinshi graduates held heavy sway, and provincial graduates were mostly treated as inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi holders commanded great prestige then, and men of provincial rank were often treated as lesser.

sentences.zh: 允成體貌魁梧，才氣飆發，欲淩甲科出其上，首疏論遼左失事諸臣，請正刑辟。

translations.literal: Yuncheng was tall and imposing in bearing, his talent and spirit soaring; wishing to rise above the jinshi and surpass them, his first memorial discussed the officials responsible for the Liaodong debacle and requested proper legal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuncheng was tall and imposing, his intellect fierce and unrestrained; determined to outshine the jinshi elite, his opening memorial addressed the officials who had lost Liaodong and demanded proper legal reckoning.

sentences.zh: 已，劾刑部尚書黃克纘倡言保護選侍，貽誤賈繼春，又曲庇盜寶內侍，至辨御史焦源溥綱常一疏，刺謬特甚。

translations.literal: Soon after, he impeached Minister of Justice Huang Kezuan for advocating protection of the Consort-in-waiting, misleading Jia Jichun, also bending the law to shield eunuchs who stole treasures, and even in rebutting Censor Jiao Yuanpu's memorial on the bonds of propriety, his distortions were especially sharp.
translations.idiomatic: He next impeached Minister of Justice Huang Kezuan for championing the Consort-in-waiting, misleading Jia Jichun, covering for treasure-stealing palace eunuchs, and rebutting Censor Jiao Yuanpu's memorial on ritual propriety with grotesque distortion.

sentences.zh: 已，極論內降及留中之害，末復規切閣部大臣。

translations.literal: Soon after, he argued at length on the harm of secret edicts from within and of keeping memorials back from the throne, and at the end again admonished the grand secretaries and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to excoriate the damage wrought by secret inner edicts and memorials withheld from the throne, closing with sharp admonitions to the grand secretaries and senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，停俸。

translations.literal: Having offended the imperial will, his salary was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took offense and suspended his salary.

sentences.zh: 給事中毛士龍劾府丞邵輔忠，允成亦偕同官李希孔斥輔忠。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Mao Shilong impeached Deputy Prefect Shao Fuzhong; Yuncheng also joined his colleague Li Xikong in denouncing Fuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Mao Shilong impeached Deputy Prefect Shao Fuzhong, Wang Yuncheng joined colleague Li Xikong in condemning him.

sentences.zh: 已，極言綱紀廢弛，請戒姑息、破因循，指斥時事甚悉。

translations.literal: Soon after, he spoke at length that discipline had collapsed, requesting caution against indulgence and breaking free of inertia, and pointed out current affairs in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued a sweeping indictment of collapsed discipline, urging an end to indulgence and bureaucratic inertia, with detailed condemnation of the reign's ills.

sentences.zh: 當是時，中貴劉朝、魏進忠與乳媼客氏相倚為奸。

translations.literal: At that time the favored eunuchs Liu Chao and Wei Jinzhong relied on each other in wickedness with the wet nurse Madam Ke.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the powerful eunuchs Liu Chao and Wei Jinzhong colluded with the wet nurse Madam Ke in a triangle of corruption.

sentences.zh: 允成抗疏歷數其罪，略言：「內廷顧命之珰，犬食其余，不蒙帷蓋之澤；

translations.literal: Yuncheng submitted a defiant memorial enumerating their crimes, saying in summary: "The eunuch entrusted at the deathbed within the inner court gets the leftovers the dogs eat, without receiving the shade of the carriage canopy;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuncheng filed a defiant memorial cataloguing their crimes, writing in part: "The deathbed eunuch within the palace receives only what the dogs leave behind, denied even the shelter of the imperial canopy;

sentences.zh: 外廷顧命之老，中旨趣出，立見田裏之收。

translations.literal: the elder entrusted at the deathbed in the outer court receives a secret edict summoning him out, and immediately one sees him harvesting in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: the deathbed minister in the outer court receives a secret summons from within—and is promptly dismissed to tend his fields.

sentences.zh: 以小馬為馳騁之貲，誰啟盤於遊田之漸；

translations.literal: with a small horse as means for galloping about, who opened the first step toward hunting excursions on the royal park's plateaus;
translations.idiomatic: A small horse becomes license for reckless galloping—who opened the first breach toward dissolute hunting in the royal parks?

sentences.zh: 以大臣為釋忿之地，誰啟咈其耇長之心。

translations.literal: with great ministers as a place to vent resentment, who opened the affront to the hearts of the elders.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers become targets for petty vindictiveness—who first taught the sovereign to defy his most venerable counselors?

sentences.zh: 劉朝輩初亦不預外事，自沈纮、邵輔忠導之，遂恣肆無忌。

translations.literal: Liu Chao and his ilk at first also did not involve themselves in outer affairs; since Shen Hong and Shao Fuzhong guided them, they then rampaged without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao and his kind had once kept clear of outer affairs—until Shen Hong and Shao Fuzhong showed them the way, and they grew utterly unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 浸假而王心一、倪思輝、朱欽相斥矣，浸假而司空用陪推矣，浸假而中旨用考官矣。

translations.literal: Gradually Wang Xinyi, Ni Sihui, and Zhu Qinxiang were driven out; gradually the Minister of Works was used for attendant promotion; gradually secret edicts were used to appoint examiners.
translations.idiomatic: In time Wang Xinyi, Ni Sihui, and Zhu Qinxiang were expelled; in time the Minister of Works was enlisted for ceremonial promotion duties; in time examiners were appointed by secret edict.

sentences.zh: 是易置大臣之權在二豎也。

translations.literal: Thus the power to replace great ministers lay in the hands of two boys.
translations.idiomatic: The power to install and dismiss great ministers had fallen to two upstart eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 近者弄權愈甚，逐大臣如振落，王紀、滿朝薦並削職為編氓。

translations.literal: Recently they have wielded power ever more fiercely, driving out great ministers as if shaking leaves from a tree; Wang Ji and Man Chaojian were both stripped of office and reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Of late their grip on power has tightened still further; ministers are cast out like leaves in a gale. Wang Ji and Man Chaojian were both demoted to the ranks of commoners.

sentences.zh: 是驅除大臣之權在二豎也。

translations.literal: Thus the power to drive out great ministers lay in the hands of two boys.
translations.idiomatic: The power to purge great ministers had fallen to two upstart eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 科臣遷改，自有定敘，給假推升，往例皆然。

translations.literal: The transfer and reassignment of censorial officials had fixed rules of seniority; promotion on leave of absence followed precedent in every case.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial appointments followed a fixed order of seniority, and promotion during leave had always been governed by established precedent.

sentences.zh: 乃惡周朝瑞之正直，忽有不許推用之旨。

translations.literal: Yet because they hated Zhou Chaorui's uprightness, there suddenly came an edict forbidding his promotion.
translations.idiomatic: But because they detested Zhou Chaorui's integrity, an edict suddenly barred him from advancement.

sentences.zh: 是轉遷百官之權在二豎也。

translations.literal: Thus the power to transfer and rotate the hundred officials lay in the hands of two boys.
translations.idiomatic: The power to shuffle the entire bureaucracy had likewise fallen to those two eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 秦藩以小宗繼大宗，諸子不得封郡王，祖制昭然。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, as the lesser line inheriting the greater, could not ennoble his sons as commandery princes—the ancestral institution was plain.
translations.idiomatic: When a minor princely line inherited the major line, as with the Prince of Qin, sons could not be ennobled as commandery princes. The ancestral rule was explicit.

sentences.zh: 乃部科爭之不獲，相繼而去。

translations.literal: Yet when the ministry and censorial offices disputed this and failed to prevail, they resigned one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry and the censorate contested the point and lost, they resigned in succession.

sentences.zh: 是進退諸藩之權在二豎也。

translations.literal: Thus the power to advance and dismiss the various princes lay in the hands of two boys.
translations.idiomatic: Even the power to promote or remove princes of the blood rested with the two eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 招權納賄，作福作威；

translations.literal: They monopolized power and accepted bribes, dispensing blessings and wielding terror;
translations.idiomatic: They hoarded power, took bribes, dispensed favors, and ruled by fear;

sentences.zh: 二豎弄權於外，客氏主謀於中。

translations.literal: the two boys manipulated power outside, while Madam Ke plotted within.
translations.idiomatic: the two eunuchs abused their authority at court while Madam Ke plotted from within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 王振、劉瑾之禍將復見今日。」

translations.literal: The calamities of Wang Zhen and Liu Jin would soon be seen again in our own day."
translations.idiomatic: The disasters wrought by Wang Zhen and Liu Jin were about to repeat themselves."

sentences.zh: 疏入，進忠輩切齒。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Jinzhong and his ilk gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Jinzhong and his faction seethed with hatred.

sentences.zh: 允成復特疏論秦府濫恩之謬，帝終不省。

translations.literal: Yuncheng again submitted a special memorial on the error of the Qin princedom's lavish favor, but the emperor to the end did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuncheng filed another special memorial condemning the Qin princedom's abuse of imperial favor, yet the emperor never took the point.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，允成又劾進忠，進忠益恨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, Yuncheng again impeached Jinzhong, and Jinzhong hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year three, Yuncheng impeached Jinzhong again, deepening his enmity.

sentences.zh: 明年，趙南星為吏部，知允成賢，調之於北。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhao Nanxing became Minister of Personnel, knew Yuncheng to be worthy, and transferred him to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhao Nanxing took office as Minister of Personnel, recognized Yuncheng's merit, and transferred him north.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南星被逐，御史張訥劾南星調允成非法，遂除名。

translations.literal: Before long Nanxing was driven out; Censor Zhang Ne impeached Nanxing's transfer of Yuncheng as illegal, and Yuncheng's name was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nanxing was expelled. Censor Zhang Ne charged that Nanxing's transfer of Yuncheng was unlawful, and Yuncheng was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 後給事中陳維新復劾允成貪險，詔撫按提問，坐以贓私。

translations.literal: Later Supervising Secretary Chen Weixin again impeached Yuncheng for greed and treachery; an edict ordered the grand coordinator and provincial governor to investigate, and he was convicted of embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Later Supervising Secretary Chen Weixin impeached Yuncheng again for corruption and malice. An edict ordered provincial authorities to investigate, and he was found guilty of graft.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，以允成嘗請保護皇弟，識其名，召復故官。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded to the throne, because Yuncheng had once petitioned to protect the emperor's younger brother, the emperor knew his name and summoned him back to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, he remembered Yuncheng's earlier plea to protect the imperial younger brother, recalled his name, and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 當天啟初，東林方盛，其主張聯絡者，率在言路。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign the Donglin faction was in full vigor, and those who advocated coordinated action were mostly on the remonstrance channels.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianqi years the Donglin movement was at its height, and its leaders on the remonstrance circuits worked in close concert.

sentences.zh: 允成居南，與北相應和，時貴多畏其鋒。

translations.literal: Yuncheng remained in the south and responded in harmony with the north; the powerful of the day mostly feared his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng held the southern post and answered the northern wing in concert, and many men of influence feared his sharp tongue.

sentences.zh: 然諤諤敢言，屢犯近幸，其風采足重雲。

translations.literal: Yet forthright and daring in speech, he repeatedly offended those close to the throne; his moral bearing was weighty enough to pierce the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Outspoken and fearless, he crossed the emperor's favorites again and again, yet his moral stature rose high enough to touch the clouds.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭氏謀危國本，而左袒之者，莫彰著於三王並封之事。

translations.literal: Formerly Lady Zheng plotted against the foundation of the state, and none who took her side stood out more plainly than in the affair of the simultaneous enfeoffment of the three princes.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Lady Zheng schemed against the succession itself, and nowhere did her partisans show themselves more clearly than in the simultaneous enfeoffment of the three princes.

sentences.zh: 今秉筆者不謂非也，且推其功，至與陳平、狄仁傑並。

translations.literal: Now those who wield the brush do not call this wrong, but even praise his merit, ranking him with Chen Ping and Di Renjie.
translations.idiomatic: Today the historians not only decline to call that wrong—they praise the man's service and rank him beside Chen Ping and Di Renjie.

sentences.zh: 此其說不可解也。

translations.literal: This doctrine cannot be understood.
translations.idiomatic: That interpretation defies comprehension.

sentences.zh: 當時並封未有旨，輔臣王錫爵蓋先有密疏請也。

translations.literal: At the time there was as yet no edict for simultaneous enfeoffment; the chief minister Wang Xijue had probably first submitted a secret memorial requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter began there was no edict for simultaneous enfeoffment; Grand Secretary Wang Xijue had almost certainly already petitioned for it in secret.

sentences.zh: 迨旨下禮部，而王如堅、朱維京、塗一臻、王學曾、嶽元聲、顧允成、於孔兼等苦口力爭，又共責讓錫爵於朝房。

translations.literal: Only after the edict reached the Ministry of Rites did Wang Rujian, Zhu Weijing, Tu Yizhen, Wang Xuezeng, Yue Yuansheng, Gu Yuncheng, Yu Kongjian, and others argue bitterly with every effort, and together rebuke Xijue in the court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the edict reached the Ministry of Rites did Wang Rujian, Zhu Weijing, Tu Yizhen, Wang Xuezeng, Yue Yuansheng, Gu Yuncheng, Yu Kongjian, and others fight it with desperate eloquence—and together confront Xijue in the court offices.

sentences.zh: 於是錫爵始知大義之不可違，而天下之不我予，隨上疏檢舉，而封事停也。

translations.literal: Then Xijue first understood that the great principle could not be violated and that the realm would not grant him its assent; he immediately submitted a memorial of self-accusation, and the enfeoffment matter was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Xijue grasp that the great principle could not be breached and that the empire would not indulge him. He at once memorialized in self-reproach, and the enfeoffment was stopped.

sentences.zh: 假令如堅等不死爭，不責讓，將並封之事遂以定，而子以母貴之說，且徐邀定策國老之勛。

translations.literal: Had Rujian and the others not argued to the death and not rebuked him, the simultaneous enfeoffment would have been settled, and the doctrine that the son is honored through the mother would slowly have earned the elder statesman who fixed the succession his reward.
translations.idiomatic: Had Rujian and the rest not fought to the last and not held Xijue to account, simultaneous enfeoffment would have stood, and the doctrine of elevation through the mother would gradually have secured the succession-fixing minister his laurels.

sentences.zh: 而乃飾之曰：「旋命旋引咎，事遂以止。」

translations.literal: Yet they dress it up and say, "An order was issued and blame was immediately taken; the affair therefore ceased."
translations.idiomatic: Yet they gloss it thus: "The order came and blame was instantly accepted, and so the matter ended."

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，此可為錫爵諱乎哉！

translations.literal: Alas, can this be a veil for Xijue!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—is this meant to shield Xijue from blame?

sentences.zh: 且聞錫爵語人曰：「王給事中遺悔否？」

translations.literal: Moreover it is heard that Xijue said to others, "Does Supervising Secretary Wang leave any regret behind?"
translations.idiomatic: And one hears that Xijue asked others, "Does Supervising Secretary Wang die with regrets?"

sentences.zh: 以故事關國本，諸臣稿項黃馘，終錫爵世不復起。

translations.literal: Because the affair touched the foundation of the state, the ministers suffered sun-scorched necks and sallow faces, yet in the end Xijue never again rose to office in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Because the matter struck at the succession itself, loyal officials wore themselves to the bone, yet Xijue never held office again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 不知前代之安劉、復唐者，誰厄王陵，使之不見天日乎？

translations.literal: Do they not know that among those in former ages who settled the Liu succession and restored the Tang, who was it that obstructed Wang Ling and kept him from seeing the light of day?
translations.idiomatic: Do they forget that among the men of old who secured the Liu line and restored the Tang, who ever buried Wang Ling so that he never saw daylight again?

sentences.zh: 曾剪除張柬之、桓彥範等五人，而令賫誌以沒乎？

translations.literal: Who ever cut down Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, and the other five men and made them die bearing unfulfilled resolve?
translations.idiomatic: Who ever destroyed Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, and their four companions and sent them to their graves with thwarted purpose?

sentences.zh: 臣所以折邪議者，一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason your subject refutes wicked opinion.
translations.idiomatic: That is my first reason for rejecting this corrupt reading of events.

sentences.zh: 其次，莫彰於張差闖宮之事。

translations.literal: Second, nothing stands out more plainly than the affair of Zhang Chachi's break into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Second, no case is clearer than Zhang Chachi's assault on the palace.

sentences.zh: 而秉筆者猶謂無罪也，且輕其事，而列王大臣、貫高事為辭。

translations.literal: Yet those who wield the brush still say there was no crime, and even treat the matter lightly, citing the cases of Wang Dachen and Guan Gao as arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the historians still declare the man innocent, treat the crime as trivial, and invoke the precedents of Wang Dachen and Guan Gao in his defense.

sentences.zh: 此其說又不可解也。

translations.literal: This doctrine too cannot be understood.
translations.idiomatic: That argument, too, defies comprehension.

sentences.zh: 王大臣之徒手而闖至乾清宮門也，馮保怨舊輔高拱，置刃其袖，挾使供之，非實事也。

translations.literal: Wang Dachen went empty-handed and broke through to the Gate of Heavenly Purity; Feng Bao, resenting the former chief minister Gao Gong, placed a blade in his sleeve and forced him to confess—it was not the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dachen burst through to the Gate of Heavenly Purity with empty hands. Feng Bao, nursing a grudge against former chief minister Gao Gong, hid a blade in his sleeve and coerced a confession. That was not truth—it was fabrication.

sentences.zh: 張差之梃，誰授之而誰使之乎？

translations.literal: Zhang Chachi's club—who put it in his hand, and who sent him?
translations.idiomatic: Who placed the club in Zhang Chachi's hands, and who commanded the attack?

sentences.zh: 貫高身無完膚，而詞不及張敖，故漢高得釋敖不問。

translations.literal: Guan Gao's body was not whole, yet his testimony did not implicate Zhang Ao, so Emperor Gaozu of Han released Ao and made no further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao was tortured until no inch of flesh was intact, yet his confession never touched Zhang Ao, and so Emperor Gaozu freed Ao without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 可與張差之事，造謀主使口招歷歷者比乎？

translations.literal: Can this be compared with Zhang Chachi's affair, where the plotters and instigators confessed in detail with their own mouths?
translations.idiomatic: Can that be compared with the Zhang Chachi case, where the plotters and their masters confessed point by point from their own lips?

sentences.zh: 昔寬處之以全倫，今直筆之以存實，以戒後，自兩不相妨，而奈之何欲諱之？

translations.literal: Formerly lenient treatment preserved human relations; today straight writing preserves truth to warn posterity—the two need not conflict. Why then insist on concealment?
translations.idiomatic: Once leniency preserved the bonds of kinship; now honest writing preserves truth to warn posterity. The two need not clash. Why insist on hiding what happened?

sentences.zh: 且諱之以為君父隱，可也；

translations.literal: Moreover, to conceal out of regard for lord and father may be acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Concealment out of reverence for lord and father may be defensible;

sentences.zh: 為亂賊輩隱，則何為？

translations.literal: to conceal for the sake of rebellious villains—what purpose does that serve?
translations.idiomatic: but concealment on behalf of traitors and criminals serves what end?

sentences.zh: 臣所以折邪議者，二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason your subject refutes wicked opinion.
translations.idiomatic: That is my second reason for rejecting this corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 至封後遺詔，自古未有帝崩立後者。
