translations.literal: As for the posthumous edict after ennobling the consort as empress, since antiquity no emperor at death has ever established an empress.
translations.idiomatic: As for the so-called posthumous edict issued after elevating a consort to empress, no emperor in history ever created an empress only as he lay dying.

sentences.zh: 此不過貴妃私人謀假母後之尊，以弭罪狀。

translations.literal: This was nothing but the honored consort's private scheming, borrowing the empress dowager's dignity to quell charges against her.
translations.idiomatic: It was nothing but the favored consort's private intrigue, borrowing the empress dowager's authority to smother her own guilt.

sentences.zh: 故稱遺詔，以要必行。

translations.literal: Hence they called it a posthumous edict to demand that it must be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the label "posthumous edict"—to force compliance as if it were binding law.

sentences.zh: 奈何猶稱先誌，重誣神祖，而陰為阿附傳封者開一面也？

translations.literal: How then can they still call it the late emperor's intent, again slander the Shenzu Emperor, and secretly leave an opening for those who fawned on the enfeoffment?
translations.idiomatic: How then can they still call it the late emperor's true wish, slander Shenzu anew, and quietly make room for those who abetted the enfeoffment?

sentences.zh: 臣所以折邪議者，三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason your subject refutes wicked opinion.
translations.idiomatic: That is my third reason for rejecting this corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 先帝之令德考終，自不宜謂因藥致崩，被不美之名。

translations.literal: The late emperor's fine virtue reached its end in natural death; it was altogether improper to say that medicine caused his collapse and attach an ugly name to him.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor died in virtue after a life of merit; to claim that medicine brought down his death and stain his name was wholly unjust.

sentences.zh: 而當時在內視病者，烏可於積勞積虛之後，投攻克之劑。

translations.literal: Yet those who attended him within at the time—how could they, after accumulated exhaustion and debility, administer strong attacking medicinals?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how could those attending him inside the palace, after years of exhaustion and depletion, have poured aggressive purgatives down his throat?

sentences.zh: 群議洶洶，方蓄疑慮變之深，而遽值先帝升遐，又適有下藥之事，安得不痛之恨之，疾首頓足而深望之？

translations.literal: Public debate was turbulent; suspicion and fear of sudden change were deeply stored, when suddenly the late emperor ascended to the heights, and there happened also to be the matter of administering medicine—how could men not grieve and hate, beat their heads and stamp their feet, and look on with deep expectation?
translations.idiomatic: Rumors swirled and suspicion ran deep just as the late emperor died—and at that very moment came word of forced medicine. Who could fail to grieve, rage, and cry out for justice?

sentences.zh: 乃討奸者憤激而甚其詞，庇奸者借題以逸其罰。

translations.literal: Thus those who sought to punish the wicked grew heated and exaggerated their words, while those who shielded the wicked seized the topic to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those pursuing the guilty grew furious and overwrote the facts; those shielding them seized on the uproar to evade punishment.

sentences.zh: 君父何人，臣子可以僥幸而嘗試乎？

translations.literal: What manner of man is lord and father, that a subject may experiment on him by chance?
translations.idiomatic: Lord and father is no subject for trial and error. What minister would dare treat the sovereign's life as a wager?

sentences.zh: 臣所以折邪議者，四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason your subject refutes wicked opinion.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fourth reason for rejecting this corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 先帝之繼神廟棄群臣也，兩月之內，鼎湖再號。

translations.literal: When the late emperor succeeded the Shenzong and cast off the ministers, within two months the imperial death bell sounded twice.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor had barely succeeded Shenzong and cast his ministers aside when, within two months, the throne mourned two emperors in succession.

sentences.zh: 陛下孑然一身，怙恃無托，宮禁深，狐鼠實繁，其於杜漸防微，自不得不倍加嚴慎。

translations.literal: Your Majesty stands alone with no one to rely on; the palace is deep, and foxes and rats truly abound—regarding stopping the first signs and guarding against incipient evil, one naturally could not but redouble strict caution.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty stands utterly alone, without protector or patron. The palace runs deep, and vermin multiply within it. To choke corruption at the root, extraordinary vigilance was unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 即不然，而以新天子儼然避正殿，讓一先朝宮嬪，萬世而下謂如何國體。

translations.literal: Even if not so, for a new Son of Heaven solemnly to vacate the main hall and yield it to a concubine of the previous reign—what would posterity say of the dignity of the state?
translations.idiomatic: Even setting that aside, what would posterity say of a new emperor vacating the main hall for a former concubine of his predecessor? What becomes of the dignity of the throne?

sentences.zh: 此楊漣等諸臣所以權衡輕重，亟以移宮請也。

translations.literal: This is why ministers such as Yang Lian weighed light and heavy and urgently petitioned for the moving of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Yang Lian and his colleagues weighed the stakes and urgently petitioned for the palace transfer.

sentences.zh: 宮已移矣，漣等之心事畢矣，本未嘗居以為功，何至反以為罪而禁錮之、擯逐之，是誠何心？

translations.literal: The palace had already been moved, and Lian and the others' purpose was fulfilled; they had never taken credit as merit—why then turn about and treat it as crime, imprisoning and banishing them? What mind truly lies behind this?
translations.idiomatic: The transfer was done and their purpose fulfilled; they had never claimed credit for it. Why then treat their act as crime, imprison them, and drive them away? What motive could justify that?

sentences.zh: 即選侍久侍先帝，生育公主，諸臣未必不力請於陛下，加之恩禮。

translations.literal: Even if the Attendant had long served the late emperor and borne a princess, the ministers would not necessarily have failed to petition Your Majesty vigorously to bestow favor and ceremony upon her.
translations.idiomatic: Even had Lady Attendant Li long served the late emperor and borne a princess, the ministers would surely have urged Your Majesty to honor her with due ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今陛下既安，選侍又未嘗不安，有何冤抑，而汲汲皇皇為無病之沈吟？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is already secure, and the Attendant too has never been insecure—what wrong or oppression is there, that one should hurry and bustle in feigned lament over a sickness that is not there?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is secure, and Lady Li is secure as well. What injustice demands this frantic pretense of grievance where none exists?

sentences.zh: 臣所以折邪議者，五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason your subject refutes wicked opinion.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fifth reason for rejecting this corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 抑猶有未盡者。

translations.literal: Yet there remains what has not been fully said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet more remains unsaid.

sentences.zh: 神祖與先帝所以處父子骨肉之際，仁義孝慈，本無可以置喙。

translations.literal: How the Shenzu Emperor and the late emperor handled the relations of father and son and flesh and bone—benevolence, righteousness, filial piety, and kindness—originally left no room for cavil.
translations.idiomatic: In the handling of father and son, kin and blood, Shenzu and the late emperor acted with such benevolence, righteousness, filial piety, and kindness that no reproach could rightly attach.

sentences.zh: 即當年母愛子抱，外議喧嘩，然雖有城社媒孽之奸，卒不以易祖訓立長之序，則愈足見神祖之明聖，與先帝之大孝。

translations.literal: Even in that year when the mother doted on her son and public debate clamored, though there were schemers who threatened the altars of state, in the end they did not alter the ancestral instruction to establish the eldest—thus all the more clearly showing the Shenzu Emperor's clarity and sagacity and the late emperor's great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the mother's favor and public uproar shook the court, and schemers threatened the realm itself, the ancestral rule of primogeniture held firm—proof of Shenzu's wisdom and the late emperor's filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 何足諱、何必諱，又何可諱？

translations.literal: What is worth concealing, what need be concealed, and what can be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: What is there to hide, what need to hide, and what could be hidden?

sentences.zh: 若謂言及鄭氏之過，便傷神祖之明，則我朝仁廟監國危疑，何嘗為成祖之累。

translations.literal: If to speak of Lady Zheng's fault is said to injure the Shenzu Emperor's clarity, then in our dynasty when Renzong supervised the realm amid doubt and peril, when did that ever become a stain on Chengzu?
translations.idiomatic: If mentioning Lady Zheng's fault is said to dim Shenzu's brilliance, then when Renzong governed amid crisis during Yongle's campaigns, did that ever tarnish Chengzu's name?

sentences.zh: 而當時史臣直勒之汗青，並未聞有嫌疑之避也。

translations.literal: Yet the historians of that time wrote it straight on the green bamboo, and one never heard of evasion out of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The historians of that age wrote it plainly in the annals, and no one shrank from the truth out of delicacy.

sentences.zh: 何獨至今而立此一說，巧為奸人脫卸，使昔日不能置之罪，今日不容著之書，何可訓也！

translations.literal: Why alone today establish this doctrine, artfully absolving wicked men, so that yesterday they could not be punished and today they may not be written in the books—what lesson can this teach!
translations.idiomatic: Why alone today invent this doctrine to absolve the guilty—so that yesterday they escaped punishment and today they must be erased from the record? What kind of moral instruction is that?

sentences.zh: 今史局開，公道明，而坐視奸輩陰謀，辨言亂義，將令三綱紊，九法滅，天下止知有私交，而不知有君父。

translations.literal: Now the historiographical bureau is open and public right is clear, yet one sits by while wicked men conspire in secret, twisting words and confounding principle, so that the three bonds will be disordered, the nine laws extinguished, and all under Heaven will know only private ties and not lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographical bureau is now at work and justice is plain, yet wicked men are allowed to conspire in silence, twisting language and corrupting principle until the three bonds unravel, law itself collapses, and the empire knows only private faction, not sovereign and father.

sentences.zh: 乞特敕纂修諸臣，據事直書，無疑無隱，則繼述大孝過於武、周，而世道人心攸賴之矣。

translations.literal: I beg a special edict to the compiling ministers to write straight according to the facts, without doubt and without concealment; then succeeding in great filial piety will surpass Wu and Zhou, and the way of the world and the hearts of men will depend upon it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg an explicit command that the compiling ministers write according to fact, without hesitation or concealment. Then the dynasty's filial succession will outshine even Wu and Zhou, and the moral order of the age will rest upon it.

sentences.zh: 詔付史館參酌，然其後卒不能改也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the History Bureau to consider it, yet afterward in the end it could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the History Bureau for deliberation, but in the end nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 已，又請出客氏於外，請誅崔文升。

translations.literal: Soon after, he again requested that Madam Ke be sent out of the palace and that Cui Wensheng be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned again to expel Madam Ke from the palace and to execute Cui Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 忌者甚眾，指為東林黨。

translations.literal: Those who resented him were very many, and pointed to him as of the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies were legion, and denounced him as a Donglin partisan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，故不與珰禍。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office, and therefore did not share in the eunuch calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office soon afterward and so escaped the eunuchs' later reign of terror.

sentences.zh: 李選侍之移宮也，其內豎劉朝、田詔、劉進忠等五人，以盜貲下刑部獄。

translations.literal: When Lady Li the Attendant moved from the palace, her inner eunuchs Liu Chao, Tian Zhao, Liu Jinzhong, and four others were sent to the Ministry of Justice prison for embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Attendant Li vacated the palace, five of her inner eunuchs—Liu Chao, Tian Zhao, Liu Jinzhong, and others—were imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice for embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 尚書黃克纘庇之，數稱其冤。

translations.literal: Minister Huang Kezuan shielded them and repeatedly declared their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Huang Kezuan shielded them and repeatedly proclaimed their innocence.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，論死。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree, and they were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and death sentences were passed.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，王安罷，魏進忠用事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year Wang An was dismissed, and Wei Jinzhong came to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: That May, Wang An was removed, and Wei Jinzhong seized control.

sentences.zh: 詔等進重賂，令其下李文盛等上疏鳴冤，進忠即傳旨貸死。

translations.literal: Zhao and the others offered heavy bribes, causing their subordinates Li Wensheng and others to submit memorials proclaiming innocence; Jinzhong immediately transmitted an edict commuting death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and his associates paid heavy bribes and had subordinates such as Li Wensheng file memorials pleading innocence. Jinzhong at once issued an edict commuting the death sentences.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉一燝等執奏者再。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries including Liu Yijiao remonstrated firmly twice.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries led by Liu Yijiao remonstrated twice, holding firm.

sentences.zh: 旨下刑科，士龍抄參者三，旨幾中寢。

translations.literal: The edict went to the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; Shilong copied the memorial for reference three times, and the edict nearly halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: The edict went to the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. Shilong submitted copied memorials for reference three times, and the order nearly stalled.

sentences.zh: 克纘乃陳其冤狀，而請付之熱審。

translations.literal: Kezuan then set forth their plea of injustice and requested that the case be sent to the summer judicial review.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan then laid out their claims of injustice and asked that the case be sent to the summer judicial review.

sentences.zh: 進忠不從，傳旨立釋。

translations.literal: Jinzhong did not agree and transmitted an edict for immediate release.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong refused and issued an edict ordering their immediate release.

sentences.zh: 士龍憤，劾克纘阿旨骫法，不可為大臣，且數朝等罪甚悉。

translations.literal: Shilong was angry and impeached Kezuan for fawning on the imperial will and bending the law, unfit to serve as a great minister, and moreover enumerated Chao and the others' crimes in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, furious, impeached Kezuan for fawning on the throne and perverting the law, declaring him unfit for high office, and detailed the crimes of Chao and the rest.

sentences.zh: 由是進忠及諸奄銜士龍次骨。

translations.literal: From this Jinzhong and the various eunuchs bore a grudge against Shilong to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment Jinzhong and the eunuchs nursed a bone-deep hatred of Shilong.

sentences.zh: 進忠廣開告密，誣天津廢將陳天爵交通李承芳，逮其一家五十余人，下詔獄。

translations.literal: Jinzhong widely opened channels for secret denunciation, falsely charging the deposed Tianjin general Chen Tianjue with communicating with Li Chengfang, and seized more than fifty members of his household, sending them to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong opened the floodgates of denunciation, falsely accusing the cashiered Tianjin general Chen Tianjue of colluding with Li Chengfang. More than fifty members of his household were seized and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 士龍即劾錦衣駱思恭及誣告者罪。

translations.literal: Shilong immediately impeached the Brocade Guard officer Luo Sigong and the false accusers for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong at once impeached Brocade Guard officer Luo Sigong and the false accusers.

sentences.zh: 進忠憾張後抑己，誣為死囚孫二所出，布散流言。

translations.literal: Jinzhong resented Empress Zhang for restraining him and falsely claimed the rumor was put about by the executed convict Sun Er, spreading the slander abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong resented Empress Zhang for holding him in check and spread slander claiming the rumor originated with the executed convict Sun Er.

sentences.zh: 士龍請究治妖言奸黨並主使逆徒，進忠益憾。

translations.literal: Shilong requested thorough punishment of seditious talk, wicked factions, and the rebellious ringleaders behind them; Jinzhong hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong demanded a full investigation of the seditious rumors, the factions behind them, and their masterminds. Jinzhong's hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 至九月，士龍劾順天府丞邵輔忠奸貪，希孔、允成亦劾之，輔忠大懼。

translations.literal: By the ninth month Shilong impeached Shao Fuzhong, deputy prefect of Shuntian, for wickedness and greed; Xikong and Yuncheng also impeached him, and Fuzhong was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month Shilong impeached Shao Fuzhong, deputy prefect of Shuntian, for corruption and greed. Li Xikong and Wang Yuncheng joined the charge, and Fuzhong was terrified.

sentences.zh: 朝等因誘以超擢，令攻士龍。

translations.literal: Chao and the others therefore tempted him with extraordinary promotion and ordered him to attack Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and his associates tempted him with promises of rapid promotion and set him against Shilong.

sentences.zh: 輔忠遂訐士龍官杭州時盜庫納妓，進忠從中下其疏。

translations.literal: Fuzhong then exposed Shilong for embezzling from the treasury and keeping courtesans while magistrate at Hangzhou; Jinzhong transmitted his memorial from within.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhong then accused Shilong of embezzling public funds and keeping courtesans while magistrate at Hangzhou. Jinzhong forwarded the memorial from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 尚書周嘉謨等言兩人所訐，風聞，請寬貸。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Jiamo and others said the mutual accusations of the two men were hearsay and requested lenient treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jiamo and others argued that the mutual accusations were hearsay and pleaded for leniency.

sentences.zh: 進忠不從，削士龍籍，輔忠落職閑住。

translations.literal: Jinzhong did not agree; Shilong's name was struck from the rolls, and Fuzhong was dismissed and ordered to reside in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong refused. Shilong was struck from the register, and Fuzhong was dismissed to idle residence.

sentences.zh: 進忠後易名忠賢，顯盜國柄，恨士龍未已。

translations.literal: Later Jinzhong changed his name to Zhongxian and openly usurped state power, his hatred of Shilong still unabated.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong later took the name Zhongxian, seized open control of the state, and still had not finished with Shilong.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，令其私人張訥劾之，再命削籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, winter, he had his private man Zhang Ne impeach him, and again ordered his name struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the fourth year, Zhongxian had his own man Zhang Ne impeach Shilong again, and the throne once more ordered his name struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 明年三月入之汪文言獄詞，謂納李三才賄三千，謀起南京吏部，下撫按提訊追贓，遣戍平陽衛。

translations.literal: The next year, in the third month, it was entered into Wang Wenyun's case confession that he had taken three thousand taels in bribes from Li Sancai and plotted to restore him to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; the case was sent to the surveillance officials for interrogation and pursuit of stolen goods, and he was exiled to Pingyang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following March, Shilong's name was woven into Wang Wenyun's confession: he had allegedly taken three thousand taels from Li Sancai and plotted to restore him to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel. The case went to provincial surveillance for interrogation and recovery of bribes, and he was banished to Pingyang Guard.

sentences.zh: 已而輔忠起用，驟遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long Fuzhong was reappointed and was suddenly promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fuzhong was brought back into service and swiftly promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月，御史劉徽復摭輔忠前奏，劾士龍納訪犯萬金，下法司逮治。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year, Censor Liu Hui again picked up Fuzhong's earlier memorial and impeached Shilong for taking ten thousand taels from a person under investigation; the case was sent to the judicial authorities for arrest and trial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year, Censor Liu Hui revived Fuzhong's old charges, accusing Shilong of taking ten thousand taels from a man under investigation. The judicial authorities were ordered to arrest and try him.

sentences.zh: 士龍知忠賢必殺己，夜中逾墻遁，其妾不知也，謂有司殺之，被發號泣於道，有司無如之何。

translations.literal: Shilong knew Zhongxian would surely kill him; in the middle of the night he climbed over the wall and fled. His concubine did not know; she thought the authorities had killed him, tore her hair loose and wailed in the road, and the officials could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong knew Zhongxian would kill him if he could. In the dead of night he scaled the wall and fled. His concubine, unaware of the escape, thought the authorities had murdered him; she tore her hair loose and wailed in the streets, and the officials were helpless to stop her.

sentences.zh: 士龍乃潛至家，載妻子浮太湖以免。

translations.literal: Shilong then stole home in secret, loaded his wife and children aboard a boat, and crossed Lake Tai to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong then slipped home in secret, put his wife and children aboard a boat, and crossed Lake Tai to safety.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，忠賢伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhongxian was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, Zhongxian was put to death.

sentences.zh: 朝士為士龍稱冤，詔盡赦其罪。

translations.literal: Court officials spoke out on Shilong's behalf, declaring his innocence, and an edict fully pardoned his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials pleaded Shilong's case, and an edict fully pardoned his offenses.

sentences.zh: 士龍始詣闕謝恩，且陳被陷之故。

translations.literal: Only then did Shilong come to court to give thanks, and set forth the reasons he had been framed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong then came to court to give thanks and explain how he had been framed.

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，命復官致仕，竟不召用。

translations.literal: The Emperor took pity on him and ordered his rank restored with retirement, yet never summoned him back to service.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took pity on him, restored his rank, and granted retirement—but never called him back to office.

sentences.zh: 至崇禎十四年，裏人周延儒再相，始起漕儲副使，督蘇、松諸郡糧。

translations.literal: Not until the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, when his fellow townsman Zhou Yanru again became chief minister, was he reappointed Deputy Commissioner for Grain Transport, overseeing grain in Su, Song, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Chongzhen 14, when his fellow townsman Zhou Yanru again became chief minister, was Shilong recalled as Deputy Commissioner for Grain Transport, supervising the grain supply of Suzhou, Songjiang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，入為太仆少卿。

translations.literal: The next winter he entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 又明年春，擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: The spring after that he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時左都御史李邦華、副都御史惠世揚皆未至，士龍獨掌院事。

translations.literal: At the time the Left Censor-in-Chief Li Banghua and the Vice Censor-in-Chief Hui Shiyang had not yet arrived; Shilong alone managed the affairs of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Li Banghua and Vice Censor-in-Chief Hui Shiyang had not yet reached the capital, so Shilong alone ran the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語輔臣：「往例御史巡方，類微服訪民間。

translations.literal: The Emperor once told his chief ministers: "By precedent, when censors toured the regions they usually went in plain dress to inquire among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once told his chief ministers: "By precedent, touring censors went in plain dress to hear the people's grievances.

sentences.zh: 近高牙大纛，氣淩巡撫，且公署前後皆通竇納賄，每奉使，富可敵國，宜重懲。」

translations.literal: Lately they travel with lofty banners and great pennants, their air overbearing toward governors, and their official quarters front and back are riddled with holes for taking bribes; each time they go on mission they grow rich enough to rival a state. They ought to be severely punished."
translations.idiomatic: Now they go out with lofty banners and great pennants, lording it over governors; their offices are riddled with secret openings for bribes, and every mission makes them rich as a kingdom. They deserve severe punishment."

sentences.zh: 士龍聞，劾逮福建巡按李嗣京。

translations.literal: When Shilong heard this, he impeached and had arrested Li Sijing, the touring censor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Shilong impeached Li Sijing, the Fujian touring censor, and had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 十月謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he retired citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he retired, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 國變後卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic upheaval he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after the fall of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：滿朝薦，健令也，出死力以抗兇鋒，幽深牢而弗悔。

translations.literal: In praise: Man Chaojian was a man of vigorous command; he exerted his utmost strength against fierce assault, and in the deepest dungeon never repented.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Man Chaojian was a man of fierce resolve. He spent his utmost strength against a murderous onslaught and, shut in the darkest prison, never repented.

sentences.zh: 及躋言路，益發憤時事，庶幾強立不反者歟。

translations.literal: Once he entered the remonstrance path, he grew ever more indignant at the affairs of the day—perhaps one who stood firm and did not bend back?
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up the censor's path, his outrage at the times only deepened—perhaps a man who stood firm and would not bend back.

sentences.zh: 江秉謙、侯震旸之論經撫，李希孔之論「三案」，皆切中事理。

translations.literal: Jiang Bingqian's and Hou Zhenyáng's arguments on provincial governors and grand coordinators, and Li Xikong's arguments on the "Three Cases," all struck the heart of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bingqian and Hou Zhenyáng on provincial governors and grand coordinators, and Li Xikong on the "Three Cases"—all hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 王允成直攻劉朝、魏進忠，而不與楊、左、周、黃諸人同難。

translations.literal: Wang Yuncheng attacked Liu Chao and Wei Jinzhong directly, yet did not share the same ordeal as Yang, Zuo, Zhou, Huang, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuncheng assailed Liu Chao and Wei Jinzhong head-on, yet did not suffer the same fate as Yang, Zuo, Zhou, Huang, and their fellows.

sentences.zh: 毛士龍顧以譎免。

translations.literal: Mao Shilong, by contrast, escaped through craft.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shilong, by contrast, slipped away through cunning.

sentences.zh: 蓋忠賢殺人皆成於附閹邪黨，彼其甘心善類，授之刃而假手焉且加功者，罪直浮於忠賢已。

translations.literal: For Zhongxian's killings all succeeded through the eunuch-adoring evil faction; they were only too glad to destroy good men—handing over the blade and killing by another's hand, even claiming merit for it—their guilt plainly outweighs Zhongxian's already.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian's killings succeeded only because the eunuch-adoring faction was eager to destroy good men—putting the blade in others' hands and even claiming credit for the deed. Their guilt plainly exceeds Zhongxian's own.
